article_title: Next-Level, Robotic Telescope-Based Observing Experiences to Boost STEM Enrollments and Majors on a National Scale
citation: Daniel E. Reichart. (2021). Next-Level, Robotic Telescope-Based Observing Experiences to Boost STEM Enrollments and Majors on a National Scale. https://tinyurl.com/skynet-workshop
title: MWU!: eight multi-wavelength observing modules adapting ERIRA for scalable classroom use
description: MWU! ("Astrophotography of the Multi-Wavelength Universe!") is a DoD-funded curriculum of "eight new observing experiences (three optical, three radio, and two capstone experiences involving both)" based on ERIRA's manual observing experiences but delivered through Skynet so they can serve orders of magnitude more students than a field experience. The modules reinforce next-level astronomy course content on stars, galaxies, and their multi-wavelength emission and absorption mechanisms, and are being co-produced and trialed by 26 participating educators in two weekly meeting groups, with a deep evaluation of effectiveness planned alongside national scaling.
requirements: Skynet access including newly integrated radio telescopes
educator participant program to produce and trial modules
constraints: Scaling and evaluation are in progress; only the first and fourth modules are being tackled in year one, and one semester of progress is reported
target_learners: pre-major-decision undergraduates in next-level astronomy courses
target_learning_goals: understanding thermal and non-thermal emission mechanisms
examples: Module 1 has students photometer thousands of stars in cluster images, plot HR diagrams, and fit isochrone models to date clusters; Module 4 has them detect pulsar polarization by period-folding radio data
key_sources: Daniel E. Reichart. (2021). Next-Level, Robotic Telescope-Based Observing Experiences to Boost STEM Enrollments and Majors on a National Scale. https://tinyurl.com/skynet-workshop

article_title: Next-Level, Robotic Telescope-Based Observing Experiences to Boost STEM Enrollments and Majors on a National Scale: Year 1 Report
citation: Daniel E. Reichart, Joshua Haislip, Vladimir Kouprianov, Ruide Fu, Logan Selph, Shengjie Xu, John Torian, Jonathan Keohane, Daryl Janzen, David Moffett, Stanley Converse. (2022). Next-Level, Robotic Telescope-Based Observing Experiences to Boost STEM Enrollments and Majors on a National Scale: Year 1 Report. https://openpress.usask.ca/skynet/chapter/hr-diagrams/
title: Team-based multi-wavelength observing modules in which students acquire, calibrate, and model their own telescope data
description: MWU! modules follow a recurring instructional pattern: students "break into teams and each team uses Skynet" to acquire their own multi-wavelength images, measure and calibrate quantities from them, plot and fit models (e.g., HR diagrams with isochrone models to date star clusters), and combine images into deep color pictures to build physical intuition about stellar populations, nebulae, pulsars, and galaxy evolution. Module 7's galaxy imaging serves as the capstone, consolidating skills from multiple modules.
requirements: Requires access to the Skynet robotic telescope network and the AgA analysis application with calibrated photometry
examples: In Module 2, teams measure the brightness of every detectable star, plot HR diagrams, fit isochrone models to date the cluster, and combine images into a single deep color picture.
key_sources: Daniel E. Reichart, Joshua Haislip, Vladimir Kouprianov, Ruide Fu, Logan Selph, Shengjie Xu, John Torian, Jonathan Keohane, Daryl Janzen, David Moffett, Stanley Converse. (2022). Next-Level, Robotic Telescope-Based Observing Experiences to Boost STEM Enrollments and Majors on a National Scale: Year 1 Report. https://openpress.usask.ca/skynet/chapter/hr-diagrams/

article_title: Skynet's "Astrophotography of the Multi-Wavelength Universe!" Curriculum
citation: Reichart, D. E. (2024). Skynet's "Astrophotography of the Multi-Wavelength Universe!" Curriculum. https://tinyurl.com/mwu-syllabus
title: MWU! multi-wavelength observing curriculum integrating optical, radio, and archival infrared data
description: MWU! is an observation-based astronomy curriculum built on the Skynet robotic telescope network, developed with a $3M DoD STEM award as a follow-up to the OPIS! curriculum. As the article states, "MWU! consists of observing experiences that integrate optical and radio, as well as archival infrared data," with inquiry topics spanning solar system objects, star formation and death, galaxies, and light-producing mechanisms. "Astrophotography serves as this curriculum's 'hook'." Modules are linked through an example syllabus.
requirements: Access to Skynet robotic telescopes and the Afterglow image-processing application, with module versions linked via the example syllabus
constraints: Much of Module 2 can be carried out without Skynet telescope access, but other modules depend on telescope time and observability of targets
target_learners: students from elementary-school level through graduate-school level in STEM pipeline programs
target_learning_goals: multi-wavelength astronomical observing and image analysis
radio astronomy on an equal footing with optical astronomy
examples: Module 3 students carry out a deep LRGB+NB observation of a star-forming region plus a small radio map looking for bremsstrahlung emission
key_sources: Reichart, D. E. (2024). Skynet's "Astrophotography of the Multi-Wavelength Universe!" Curriculum. https://tinyurl.com/mwu-syllabus
